text: At site LS-1, two structures are built: landing pad PAD1 in zone Z1 and blast berm BERM1 in zone Z2. Two excavators (EX1, EX2) handle digging, though only EX1 is used; two haulers (HL1, HL2) move regolith, with HL2 assigned; one compactor (CP1) prepares surfaces; one printer (PR1) sinters regolith; and one surveyor (SV1) stakes and inspects. Work proceeds with strict zone isolation: only one robot operates in Z1 or Z2 at a time due to plume safety. Precedence constraints require surveying before excavation, compaction before sintering, and full inspection before pad sign-off. The critical path runs 72 hours, well under the 336-hour horizon. Battery limits are respected: SV1 uses 462 Wh total (under 1500 Wh), HL2 uses 840 Wh (under 3000 Wh), EX1 uses 2010.6 Wh (under 5000 Wh), CP1 uses 1896.6 Wh (under 3500 Wh), and PR1 uses 3948.8 Wh (under 4000 Wh), making printer energy the tightest constraint. The solver verified an optimal schedule with zero conflicts, confirming all tasks complete within energy, zone, and precedence limits.
